display.purpose: Headlines, the wordmark, question stems, archetype names, and the oversized coral numerals. Weights 600-900, letter-spacing -0.03em, line-height 0.92-1.2. Never used for reading text.

body.purpose: Reading copy, button labels, and every control. 13-17px at line-height 1.6-1.7.

data.purpose: Counts, scale labels, proficiency bands, eyebrows, and footers. 8-11px, uppercase, letter-spacing 0.04-0.12em. Carries anything the scouting report treats as a measurement.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: The only easing curve in the system. Fast out of the gate, long settle — used on every transition.

motion.name: duration-state
motion.purpose: Hover and selection feedback on cards, scale points, and nav items. Fast enough to feel mechanical rather than animated.

motion.name: duration-action
motion.purpose: The primary coral button's background shift. Slightly slower than state feedback because it is the page's single committing action.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: transition: none !important; animation: none !important; scroll-behavior: auto
motion.purpose: Under prefers-reduced-motion the system drops all transitions and smooth scrolling. Nothing in the system depends on motion to convey state — selection is carried by color and border, so removal is lossless.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The single committing action on a screen: start the quiz, advance a question, copy a result link. Square, coral, with the arrow pushed to the far edge by a wide gap.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { min-height: 56px; padding: 16px 24px; border: 0; border-radius: 0; background: var(--coral-500, #f0485c); color: var(--ink-900, #0d0d0d); display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; gap: 28px; font-family: 'Barlow', sans-serif; font-size: 15px; font-weight: 700; cursor: pointer; transition: background 200ms cubic-bezier(.2,0,.2,1); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: var(--coral-600, #d93a4e); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--coral-500, #f0485c); outline-offset: 4px; } .ds-btn-primary:disabled { opacity: .4; cursor: not-allowed; } .ds-btn-arrow { font: 500 24px/1 'Barlow', sans-serif; }

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: The header's persistent quiz entry. A coral hairline outline with white label; the fill only appears on hover, and then only at 12% opacity.
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { padding: 9px 16px; border: 1px solid var(--coral-500, #f0485c); border-radius: 0; background: transparent; color: #fff; font-family: 'Barlow', sans-serif; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: .04em; white-space: nowrap; cursor: pointer; transition: background 120ms cubic-bezier(.2,0,.2,1); } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { background: rgba(240,72,92,.12); } .ds-btn-ghost:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--coral-500, #f0485c); outline-offset: 4px; }

components.name: Text Button
components.description: The always-available retreat: previous question, take it again. Underlined at a 5px offset in muted grey, brightening to white on hover. Never competes with the coral action beside it.
components.css: .ds-btn-text { padding: 12px 0; border: 0; background: transparent; color: var(--paper-500, #7c7c7c); font-family: 'Barlow', sans-serif; font-size: 13px; text-decoration: underline; text-underline-offset: 5px; cursor: pointer; transition: color 120ms cubic-bezier(.2,0,.2,1); } .ds-btn-text:hover { color: #fff; } .ds-btn-text:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--coral-500, #f0485c); outline-offset: 4px; }

components.name: Scale Point
components.description: The signature control. Five of these sit in an equal-width row as the answer scale. A hollow ring fills solid when chosen and the whole tile inverts to coral — selection reads from across the room, and reads without color alone because the dot fills too.
components.css: .ds-scale { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(3, minmax(0,1fr)); gap: 8px; } .ds-scale-point { min-height: 96px; padding: 16px 8px; border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.14); border-radius: 0; background: var(--ink-700, #1a1a1a); color: var(--paper-300, #b4b4b4); display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; text-align: center; cursor: pointer; transition: background 120ms cubic-bezier(.2,0,.2,1), border-color 120ms cubic-bezier(.2,0,.2,1), color 120ms cubic-bezier(.2,0,.2,1); } .ds-scale-point:hover { background: var(--ink-600, #232323); border-color: var(--paper-500, #7c7c7c); color: #fff; } .ds-scale-point:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--coral-500, #f0485c); outline-offset: 4px; } .ds-scale-point--selected { background: var(--coral-500, #f0485c); border-color: var(--coral-500, #f0485c); color: var(--ink-900, #0d0d0d); } .ds-scale-point--selected:hover { background: var(--coral-600, #d93a4e); border-color: var(--coral-600, #d93a4e); color: var(--ink-900, #0d0d0d); } .ds-scale-dot { width: 16px; height: 16px; border: 2px solid currentColor; border-radius: 50%; display: block; } .ds-scale-point--selected .ds-scale-dot { background: currentColor; } .ds-scale-label { font: 500 11px/1.3 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace; }

components.name: Trait Row
components.description: One line of the nine-trait scorecard: display-face label, a flat 8px coral bar with no radius, and the proficiency band set in mono, right-aligned. Rows are separated by hairlines only — the scorecard reads as a table, not a set of cards.
components.html:
SlashingExcellent
VisionSolid
components.css: .ds-trait-list { border-top: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.14); } .ds-trait-row { min-height: 52px; border-bottom: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.14); display: grid; grid-template-columns: 8rem minmax(0,1fr) 6rem; align-items: center; gap: 16px; } .ds-trait-label { color: #fff; font: 600 14px 'Archivo', sans-serif; } .ds-trait-bar { height: 8px; background: var(--ink-600, #232323); display: block; overflow: hidden; } .ds-trait-fill { height: 100%; background: var(--coral-500, #f0485c); display: block; } .ds-trait-band { color: var(--paper-300, #b4b4b4); font: 500 10px/1.3 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace; letter-spacing: .04em; text-align: right; text-transform: uppercase; }

components.name: Instinct Card
components.description: The role cards on the landing page. Depth comes from a single tonal step above the section band and nothing else — no border, no shadow. The circled mono numeral is the one curve in the system.
components.html:
01

Creator

Vision · Shot Creation
components.css: .ds-card { min-height: 180px; max-width: 260px; background: var(--ink-700, #1a1a1a); border-radius: 0; padding: 22px; display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: flex-start; gap: 14px; transition: background 120ms cubic-bezier(.2,0,.2,1); } .ds-card:hover { background: var(--ink-600, #232323); } .ds-circle-number { width: 26px; height: 26px; border: 1px solid var(--paper-500, #7c7c7c); border-radius: 50%; display: inline-grid; place-items: center; flex: none; color: var(--paper-300, #b4b4b4); font: 500 10px/1 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace; } .ds-card-title { margin: 0; color: #fff; font: 700 19px/1.2 'Archivo', sans-serif; letter-spacing: -.03em; } .ds-card-body { margin: 0; color: var(--paper-500, #7c7c7c); font-family: 'Barlow', sans-serif; font-size: 13px; line-height: 1.6; }

components.name: Navigation Item
components.description: Header navigation. Each item pairs a circled mono numeral with a small Barlow label, so the nav reads as a numbered sequence rather than a list of links.
components.css: .ds-nav { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 34px; } .ds-nav-item { border: 0; background: none; color: var(--paper-300, #b4b4b4); display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; font-family: 'Barlow', sans-serif; font-size: 12px; cursor: pointer; transition: color 120ms cubic-bezier(.2,0,.2,1); } .ds-nav-item:hover { color: #fff; } .ds-nav-item:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--coral-500, #f0485c); outline-offset: 4px; } .ds-circle-number { width: 26px; height: 26px; border: 1px solid var(--paper-500, #7c7c7c); border-radius: 50%; display: inline-grid; place-items: center; flex: none; color: var(--paper-300, #b4b4b4); font: 500 10px/1 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace; }

components.name: Progress Meter
components.description: A 2px full-bleed coral rule under the quiz topline. It is the only progress affordance in the product and it never becomes a bar with a container, a percentage, or a radius.
components.css: .ds-progress { width: 100%; height: 2px; margin: 0; appearance: none; border: 0; background: var(--ink-500, #2e2e2e); display: block; } .ds-progress::-webkit-progress-bar { background: var(--ink-500, #2e2e2e); } .ds-progress::-webkit-progress-value { background: var(--coral-500, #f0485c); } .ds-progress::-moz-progress-bar { background: var(--coral-500, #f0485c); }

narrative.overview:
Court Type looks like a scouting report printed on near-black newsprint. The system carries itself with the flat authority of a document that measures someone: oversized Archivo headlines that crop tight against the baseline, monospace numerals treating every count as data, and hairline rules doing the work that borders and shadows would do in a softer system. Nothing is rounded, nothing is lifted, and nothing is decorated.

Depth is entirely tonal. Four near-black surfaces — #0d0d0d, #141414, #1a1a1a, #232323 — step upward by a few percent of lightness each, and a 1px white rule at 14% opacity separates what the tonal step alone cannot. There is not a single box-shadow in the system, and the only curve is the 50% circle on a mono numeral.

One coral does all the persuading. It fills the committing button, marks the selected answer, draws every progress and trait bar, names the archetype, and outlines focus. Because it appears nowhere else, its presence on a screen is unambiguous instruction: this is the thing to press, or this is the thing you scored.
keyCharacteristics: Square by default — the only border-radius in the system is 50% on circled numerals
Flat by default — zero box-shadows; depth is four tonal steps of near-black plus hairline rules
One coral accent (#f0485c) reserved for action, selection, measurement, and focus
Three fonts with strict jobs: Archivo displays, Barlow reads, IBM Plex Mono measures
Monochrome photography, always shaded so display type stays legible over it
Asymmetric editorial splits — 28/72 on the quiz, 36/64 on the result — divided by a single vertical rule

rules.name: The One Coral Rule
rules.body: Coral marks action, selection, measurement, and focus — nothing else. It never becomes a decorative fill, a section background, or a second text color. Its scarcity is what makes the primary button unmissable.

rules.name: The Tonal Depth Rule
rules.body: Surfaces separate by a tonal step and a hairline, never by a shadow. If two planes are not distinguishable, move one a step along the ink scale or add a 1px rule at rgba(255,255,255,.14) — do not reach for elevation.

rules.name: The Square Corner Rule
rules.body: Every rectangle in the system has a 0px radius: buttons, cards, tiles, bars, inputs. The circled numeral at 50% is the sole exception, and it is a numeral, not a container.

rules.name: The Three Jobs Rule
rules.body: Archivo displays, Barlow reads, IBM Plex Mono measures. A count, a scale label, a proficiency band, or an eyebrow is set in mono and uppercased; a sentence someone actually reads is never mono.

dos: Do separate surfaces with a tonal step on the ink scale (#0d0d0d → #141414 → #1a1a1a → #232323) and a 1px rule at rgba(255,255,255,.14).
Do set every count, label, band, and eyebrow in IBM Plex Mono, uppercase, with 0.04–0.12em letter-spacing.
Do give display headlines -0.03em letter-spacing and a line-height at or below 1.2 so they crop tight.
Do carry selection in both color and shape — the scale point inverts to coral and its ring fills solid, so the state survives without color.
Do shade monochrome photography with a dark gradient before setting type over it.
Do keep focus rings coral at 2px with a 4px offset, on every interactive element.
donts: Don't add a box-shadow. The system has none, and adding one breaks the printed-document flatness that everything else depends on.
Don't round a rectangle. 0px is the radius for every container; 50% belongs only to circled numerals.
Don't introduce a second accent hue. If something needs emphasis and coral is already spoken for, use white display type or a tonal step instead.
Don't set reading copy in IBM Plex Mono, or a measurement in Barlow.
Don't use full-color photography — every image in the system is grayscale with contrast pushed and brightness pulled.
Don't rely on motion to convey state: under prefers-reduced-motion all transitions are removed, so any state that only animates is a state that disappears.
